introduction: Vermont Legal Aid and Legal Services Vermont jointly provide free civil legal help. Legal Services Vermont screens requests and assigns or refers accepted matters.
description: Vermont Legal Aid and Legal Services Vermont jointly provide free civil legal help. Legal Services Vermont screens requests and assigns or refers accepted matters.

sections.who: Eligibility depends on the issue, Vermont connection, income and resources. Current funding limits exclude many issues from callbacks; check the list before requesting help.
sections.get: Help can range from information or advice to representation in an accepted case. A request alone does not create representation.
sections.docs:
• Court papers and notices with dates.
  • Records related to the legal issue.
  • Income and household details needed for intake.
sections.apply:
1. Check the service list

    Read How We Can Help, including the current issues that cannot receive replies.

  2. Request screening

    Use its Legal Help Request Form or leave a helpline message at 800-889-2047 during listed hours.

  3. Provide safe contact details

    State the safest way to reach you and all important deadlines.
sections.after: The current provider asks applicants not to leave a second message. Keep court deadlines while waiting and use the linked self-help resources.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Current joint legal intake. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Does every issue get a callback?
No. The provider publishes current exclusions due to limited staffing.
The joint service principally handles civil matters.
The provider offers interpreters without charge.
Its current instructions say not to leave a second message.
